title: Sanger sequencing: chain termination
caption: DNA polymerase copies the template, but a little ddNTP, which has no 3′–OH, is mixed in: whenever one is added, the chain stops. The result is a fragment of every length, each ending at a base marked by a coloured dye. Sorted by size, the colours of the last bases spell out the new strand.
alt: Ten fragments of a new DNA strand, one of every length from 1 to 10 bases, each ending in a coloured base; reading the last bases from shortest to longest gives GATTACAGCT.
description: The template is copied by DNA polymerase from a primer, using normal dNTPs and a little labelled ddNTP.
Whenever a ddNTP is added the chain stops, so fragments of every length are made.
Fragments are separated by size by capillary electrophoresis, and a laser reads the dye of each last base.
From the shortest fragment upwards the last bases read GATTACAGCT.
The template strand is the complement: CTAATGTCGA.
